content:
The Observatory said winds in Hong Kong will strengthen. At 8:10 p.m., the government has notified employees with long commutes to leave work, and reminded members of the public whose journeys home are long, complicated, or who live on outlying islands to start heading home.

On Saturday afternoon, the Strong Wind Signal No. 3 was in effect. Typhoon Saola took the lead in making its presence felt. At around 4 p.m., the weather deteriorated, with wind and rain beginning. At a construction site at 750 Cheung Sha Wan Road in Lai Chi Kok, a giant scaffold was blown down in the wind and rain. The scaffold, about five storeys tall, toppled over, with part of it falling onto the rooftop of a nearby industrial building. Fire services dispatched a disaster response and rescue vehicle, and ambulances arrived at the scene. Police officers at the site wore helmets and maintained order at a nearby bus stop. No injuries were reported initially.

During the typhoon, members of the public queued up at stalls in Kowloon City Market to buy vegetables and beef. At a construction site, workers left the tower crane area and returned to a safe location at around 2 p.m.

The Observatory said this afternoon that at 4 p.m., Typhoon Saola was centred about 250 kilometres east-southeast of Hong Kong, moving at around 18 kilometres per hour, and is forecast to move northwest towards the coast of eastern Guangdong in general. The Observatory will assess, depending on Saola's landfall location and distance from Hong Kong, the size of the gale zone, and local wind conditions, whether a higher tropical cyclone warning signal needs to be issued between 9 p.m. and midnight tonight.
